title: Individual assessment of genetic sarcoma susceptibility in children, adolescents, and young adults with sarcomas
summary:
Sarcomas are malignant diseases of bone and soft tissues that occur in children, adolescents, and adults. Sarcomas can arise as a result of (likely) pathogenic germline variants in cancer predisposition genes. In published studies, cancer predisposition genes were examined in 3040 children, adolescents, and adults for the presence of (probably) pathogenic germline variants. Thereby, (probably) pathogenic variants in defined cancer predisposition genes were found in 7-27% of all examined patients. The vast majority of these gene variants were monoallelic. The most frequently affected genes were TP53, NF1, the mismatch repair genes MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2, as well as BRCA1/2 and other Fanconi anemia genes. Based on a thorough review, we identified 117 cancer predisposition genes for which (likely) pathogenic germline variants have been described in sarcoma patients.

The aim of this research project is to detect (likely) pathogenic germline variants in cancer predisposition genes in children, adolescents, and young adults with sarcoma and to test the following questions:

(a) How reliably does clinical history evidence of genetic predisposition to sarcoma correlate with the presence of (likely) pathogenic germline variants in cancer predisposition genes ? Possible clinical anamnestic indications of a genetic predisposition to sarcoma are examined with the help of the Sarcoma Predisposition Checklist of the German Cancer Society. The checklist was based on a thorough review of the published literature on genetic sarcoma predisposition.

b) Does the frequency of (likely) pathogenic germline variants in cancer predisposition genes differ in different age groups?
conditions: Malignant neoplasms of bone and articular cartilage
Malignant neoplasms of mesothelial and soft tissue

interventions.name: Peripheral blood and/ or buccal swabs will be taken from all study patients for DNA extraction and subsequent whole exome sequencing (WES).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Prior diagnosis of a bone or soft-tissue sarcoma,
Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
No diagnosis of sarcoma,
Lack of informed consent
